task_title: Project-owned grid A* replacing rot-js Path.AStar in findTilePath

plan_review.notes: Adversarial rubber-duck review returned REJECT-as-specified with 3 blocking + 4 non-blocking findings and 3 alternatives (keep rot-js and only swap the closed set; stable bucketed monotone priority queue instead of a heap; upstream a patch to rot-js). Blocking fixes forced into the design: (1) findTilePath keeps a rot-js fallback for non-integer coordinates because TileMap.inBounds accepts them; (2) the passability predicate must be probed for all four N/E/S/W neighbours before any enqueue, matching rot-js _getNeighbors, because isTilePassable is caller-supplied and not required to be pure; (3) validation must diff probe traces, not just returned paths. Divergence is minor: the heap+typed-array core survived, two compatibility constraints were added. Alternative 1 was priced empirically as the CLOSEDSET bench variant (6.12x vs 8.42x) and rejected as leaving half the win on the table; alternative 2 deferred pending that measurement; alternative 3 rejected as unshippable on this timeline.

rounds.notes: Line-by-line audit against rot-js 2.2.1 semantics read directly from node_modules. Attacked heap sift-up/sift-down FIFO fidelity, generation-stamp aliasing across same-tile-count/different-shape maps, MAX_GENERATION wrap, prevTile-chain vs item.prev-object-chain equivalence under duplicate pushes, the y*width+x index guard against a predicate returning true for x=-1, scratch-pool reentrancy and throw safety, Int32 range, the non-integer fallback, and test vacuity. No counterexample found. Independently re-ran the equivalence suite (31/31) and the differential oracle (4350 comparisons byte-identical).
